title: Satya Nadella × xAI: Grok on Azure
summary: Deal discussion on distributing Grok 5 for enterprise through Azure AI Foundry. Agreed in principle: Grok 5 joins Foundry's model catalog with enterprise SLAs, sold through Microsoft's enterprise channel with revenue share; inference runs on Azure capacity while all training stays on Colossus; hard contractual wall between Grok enterprise traffic and any Microsoft model training. Grok will also be an optional model behind Copilot for specific workloads, pending benchmark gates. Consumer Grok and the X integration stay exclusively with xAI.
decisions: Grok 5 enterprise joins the Azure AI Foundry model catalog with full enterprise compliance SLAs
Inference on Azure capacity; all Grok training remains on xAI's Colossus clusters
Contractual and technical isolation: no Grok enterprise traffic is used for training by either party
Grok becomes an optional backend model for specific Copilot workloads, gated on benchmark parity reviews
Consumer Grok and the X platform integration remain exclusive to xAI
Revenue share on Foundry sales follows the standard third-party model split, with a floor renegotiated at $1B run-rate

action_items.task: Send the Foundry onboarding package: compliance matrix, SLA templates, and the isolation architecture review process
Deliver Grok 5 enterprise benchmark results and the inference capacity requirements for launch regions
Confirm the Copilot workload list where Grok competes as backend and the parity review criteria

transcript.speaker: Satya Nadella
transcript.text: Elon, welcome to Redmond. I'll admit when my team put this meeting on the calendar there were some raised eyebrows in the building, given the ecosystem we've, let's say, historically been associated with.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Satya, half the buildings I walk into these days have raised eyebrows, it's ambient at this point. But look — the reason I'm here is simple. Grok 5 is now at or above frontier on the enterprise benchmarks that matter, and xAI has exactly zero enterprise sales motion. You have the best enterprise distribution machine in software history. I don't want to build what you already built.

transcript.speaker: Satya Nadella
transcript.text: And from my side — I have been saying publicly for two years that Azure will be the home for every frontier model, plural, and I mean it. Our customers do not want a single-model future; they want choice with enterprise guarantees around it. Foundry already carries multiple frontier families. Grok being absent is a gap in the catalog. So the strategic logic is easy. The interesting parts are the details, and Scott owns the details.

transcript.speaker: Scott Guthrie
transcript.text: So let me start with what onboarding actually means, because Foundry enterprise isn't just an API endpoint. It's SOC 2 and FedRAMP paths, EU data boundary compliance, customer-managed keys, regional data residency, ninety-nine-nine SLAs with financial penalties, and abuse monitoring that satisfies our enterprise terms. Every model family in the catalog went through it. It typically takes a quarter. That's the price of our sales force selling it.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: We'll pass it. xAI already runs government workloads, so FedRAMP-adjacent controls exist, and the EU boundary work is done for the consumer product. Send the compliance matrix and we'll turn it around fast — my team is small but it's the kind of small that ships. What I want to get precise about today is the thing that would kill this deal if we get it wrong: isolation.

transcript.speaker: Satya Nadella
transcript.text: Say exactly what you need. I'd rather over-specify this today than litigate it later — and I say that as someone with some experience in complicated AI partnerships.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Ha — yes, your other partnership is exactly why I'm being surgical. Three walls. One: no Grok enterprise traffic — prompts, outputs, telemetry — is available for training to anyone, including us, including you, including any Microsoft model team. Two: model weights deploy into confidential-computing enclaves on Azure; your ops people run the infrastructure but cannot extract the weights. Three: training never leaves Colossus. Azure gets inference. The frontier work stays in Memphis.

transcript.speaker: Scott Guthrie
transcript.text: All three are doable and honestly two of them are how the catalog already works — confidential inference enclaves are exactly how we host other third-party frontier weights, so the machinery exists and is audited annually. The no-training wall we'll paper contractually plus technically: enterprise inference traffic in Foundry is already excluded from any training by default. We'll extend the same attestation to you that customers get from us.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Good. And I want mutual audit rights, not just attestations — my security team walks your enclave architecture once a year, yours can walk our training exclusion pipeline. Trust but verify, where verify is the load-bearing word.

transcript.speaker: Satya Nadella
transcript.text: Mutual audit rights, agreed. Now let me raise the part you haven't asked about, because it's the part I actually find most interesting: Copilot. Foundry catalog access gets you enterprise API customers. But the larger prize is Copilot's daily active base. We have been moving Copilot toward model-agnostic routing — the right model per workload. If Grok wins specific workloads on our benchmarks, it can serve them behind Copilot. Real volume, hundreds of millions of users.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: That's a bigger offer than I came for, so naturally I'm suspicious. What's the catch — and what does 'wins on our benchmarks' mean, who runs them, and does your other partner get to see my scores?

transcript.speaker: Scott Guthrie
transcript.text: Fair questions. The parity reviews are run by our internal evaluation team on held-out enterprise task suites — coding, document analysis, agentic workflows. Every backend model gets the same suite, nobody sees anyone else's raw scores, and the routing decision is ours. The catch, stated plainly: you're competing against every other model in the catalog for those slots, permanently. Nobody gets tenure in Copilot.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Competing permanently on merit is the only arrangement I've ever trusted, so that's fine. Grok will take the coding and agentic slots within two quarters, and you can quote me internally. Okay — economics. What's the standard split on Foundry, and don't give me the first-offer number, give me the number you gave the other frontier labs.

transcript.speaker: Satya Nadella
transcript.text: Ha! Scott, don't answer that directly. Elon — the standard third-party split is the standard for a reason: it's what makes our sellers actually sell it, because their quota credit is identical whichever model the customer picks. That neutrality is worth more to you than five points of margin. Where I have flexibility is scale incentives: when Grok on Azure crosses a billion-dollar run-rate, the split renegotiates with a floor in your favor. Growth is the lever, not the entry price.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Standard split with a renegotiation floor at a billion run-rate — accepted, on one condition. Capacity. If Copilot routing sends Grok real volume, I need Azure inference capacity guaranteed ahead of demand, not behind it. I've spent this decade watching compute promises slip. I want committed GPU allocations per region in the contract, with the same financial penalties your SLAs put on you.

transcript.speaker: Scott Guthrie
transcript.text: We can commit launch-region capacity with penalties — that's you asking us to eat our own cooking, which is fair. I need your side of it though: real benchmark results and honest capacity projections by the 21st, because I provision against your numbers. If you tell me it's going to be huge and it's huge, we're fine. If you tell me it's huge and it's quiet, I've stranded GPUs I could have sold three times over.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: You'll have benchmarks and projections by the 21st, and I'll give you the honest number and the dream number clearly labeled, which is more than most vendors do. One thing I want stated in the room so there's no ambiguity later: consumer Grok — the X integration, the app — is not part of this. That stays ours exclusively. You're getting the enterprise product.

transcript.speaker: Satya Nadella
transcript.text: Understood and honestly preferred — the consumer surface is your brand and your risk. What I do want stated back is the mirror image: this deal is non-exclusive for us too. We continue partnering with every lab, including the one whose relationship with you keeps the technology press employed. Foundry is Switzerland. That neutrality is the entire product.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Foundry is Switzerland, agreed — I'm not asking you to pick sides, I'm asking you to sell shelf space to the best product on the shelf. My lawyers and their lawyers can keep each other company in the meantime; it's basically a jobs program at this point. And Satya, credit where due: model-agnostic was the right call and you made it before it was obvious.

transcript.speaker: Satya Nadella
transcript.text: It was obvious the day I understood that no single lab, mine included, will win every workload forever. Okay — let me summarize, because I think we have a deal shape. Grok 5 enterprise enters Foundry onboarding now: Scott's team sends the compliance matrix and isolation review by the 14th. You deliver benchmarks and capacity projections by the 21st. I confirm the Copilot workload list and parity criteria by the 28th. Standard split, billion-dollar renegotiation floor, committed capacity with penalties, three isolation walls with mutual audits, consumer stays yours, Foundry stays neutral.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: That's the deal. Target announcement at your Ignite conference in November — enterprise theater is your home turf, and I'll be somewhat busy that month landing robots on Mars anyway.

transcript.speaker: Satya Nadella
transcript.text: Ignite works. And Elon — genuinely — good luck in November. Everyone in this industry argues about everything, but I don't know a single person who isn't rooting for those ships. Land them, and then come do a keynote about what Grok does with a second planet's worth of data.
